original_value: Timely detection and diagnosis are essentially needed to guide outbreak measures and infection control. It is vital to improve healthcare quality in public places, markets, schools and airports and provide useful insights into the technological environment and help researchers acknowledge the choices and gaps available in this field. In this narrative review, the detection of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) technologies is summarized and discussed with a comparison between them from several aspects to arrive at an accurate decision on the feasibility of applying the best of these techniques in the biosensors that operate using laser detection technology. The collection of data in this analysis was done by using six reliable academic databases, namely, Science Direct, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and PubMed. This review includes an analysis review of three highlights: evaluating the hazard of pandemic COVID-19 transmission styles and comparing them with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) to identify the main causes of the virus spreading, a critical analysis to diagnose coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) based on artificial intelligence using CT scans and CXR images and types of biosensors. Finally, we select the best methods that can potentially stop the propagation of the coronavirus pandemic.

result.paraphrase: Timely detection and diagnosis are essential for guiding outbreak control and infection prevention. Improving healthcare quality in public settings such as markets, schools, and airports is vital, and doing so can offer valuable insight into the technological landscape while helping researchers identify the options and gaps in this field. This narrative review summarizes and discusses COVID-19 detection technologies, comparing them across multiple aspects to reach an accurate judgment on the feasibility of applying the best of these techniques in laser-detection biosensors. Data for this analysis were gathered from six reputable academic databases: Science Direct, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and PubMed. The review analyzes three key points: assessing the risk of COVID-19 transmission patterns and comparing them with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) to determine the main drivers of viral spread; critically examining artificial-intelligence-based COVID-19 diagnosis using CT scans and CXR images, along with biosensor types; and, finally, selecting the most effective methods that could help halt the spread of the coronavirus pandemic.
